title: Global Integration Crisis — Mega
summary: Idempotency, retries, certs, DLQ — taught step-by-step then applied to duplicate orders.

knownLimitations: Verify live details in SAP docs

steps.title: How Odyssey teaches
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Learn → Check → Do → Evidence
teach.explain: Every micro-step teaches a concept, checks understanding, then asks you to apply it on a simulated landscape. Mastery is evidence, not XP. Simulation fidelity is Tier 2 — labeled, not live SAP.
teach.analogy: Flight simulator: procedures are real; the aircraft is synthetic.
teach.whyItMatters: Skipping teaching panels creates cargo-cult clicking.
formalPoints: Read teach panel before answering checks
commonMistakes: Rushing to fix without reading symptoms

check.question: What is the correct learning order in Odyssey?

options.text: Learn concept → check understanding → apply on simulation → capture evidence
Click fix until green, ignore panels

options.feedback: Checks help, but application and diagnosis are required.

check.explanation: Odyssey is deliberate practice with evidence, not a slot machine.

steps.title: Fidelity honesty
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: What this simulator is (and is not)
teach.explain: Tier 2 behavioral simulation models major inputs/outputs/failures with simplifications. It does not mint real JWTs, run OpenUI5, or bill real BTP. Always verify production decisions against official SAP documentation.
teach.whyItMatters: Confusing sim with prod creates dangerous overconfidence.

check.question: A Tier 2 simulation means…

options.text: Major behaviors modeled with documented simplifications

options.feedback: That would be misleading; we never claim that.
This product is independent and not certification.

check.explanation: Honesty about fidelity is part of professional ethics.

steps.title: Business situation intake
steps.prompt: Restate business risk of duplicates.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Start from business pain, not technology fashion
teach.explain: Global order intake shows duplicates and partner TLS issues at peak.
teach.analogy: Double-stamped passports at a chaotic border.
teach.whyItMatters: Solutioneering early locks teams into the wrong platform choices.

check.question: In one or two sentences, restate the business goal and one hard constraint.
check.explanation: Restating prevents solving the wrong problem.

steps.title: Functional vs NFR
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Separate WHAT from HOW WELL
teach.explain: Functional requirements are capabilities. Non-functional requirements constrain quality: security, privacy, latency, cost, accessibility, audit. Stakeholders often hand you solutions disguised as requirements.
teach.analogy: Need: cross the river. Solution idea: buy a hovercraft. Keep them separate.
teach.whyItMatters: NFRs drive architecture more than feature lists.
commonMistakes: Accepting 'use CAP' as a requirement without the underlying need

check.question: Which is primarily an NFR?

options.text: P95 API latency under 400ms for EU users

steps.title: Stakeholder statements → needs
steps.prompt: List conflicting pressures.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Interview for constraints and evidence
teach.explain: SRE wants backoff; partner manager wants uptime; security wants cert hygiene.

check.question: Name one functional need and one NFR you heard (or inferred) and one item still missing evidence.

steps.title: Write requirements cleanly
steps.prompt: Write F / NFR / Constraints / Assumptions for this mission. Use the words functional and non-functional explicitly.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Requirements artifact
teach.explain: Produce four lists: Functional, Non-functional, Constraints, Assumptions/Open questions. This artifact feeds architecture and test design.

check.question: Paste a compact requirements list using the headers Functional and Non-functional.
check.explanation: Explicit headers prove you separated concerns.

steps.title: Global account → subaccount
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Hierarchy before heroics
teach.explain: Global account is commercial root. Subaccounts isolate projects/stages/regions. You deploy into environments under subaccounts, not into the global account itself.
teach.miniDiagram: Global Account → Directory? → Subaccount → Environment (CF/Kyma/ABAP) → Apps/Services

check.question: Where do you typically deploy a CAP app?

options.text: Into an environment under a subaccount
Directly into the global account root with no subaccount
options.feedback: Global account is not the app runtime container.
Not for CAP side-by-side cloud apps.

check.explanation: Hierarchy literacy prevents entitlement and isolation mistakes.

steps.title: CF space ≠ subaccount
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Two different isolation axes
teach.explain: Subaccounts are BTP boundaries. CF spaces are runtime groupings inside a CF environment. Using the words interchangeably confuses ops and security reviews.

check.question: A Cloud Foundry space is…

options.text: A runtime grouping for apps/service instances inside CF

check.explanation: Precise vocabulary is an operational safety tool.

steps.title: Inspect the simulated landscape
steps.prompt: List degraded resources and one dependency edge that looks suspicious. Mentions health states.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Inventory before inference
teach.explain: Open the fleet/graph. Note health, owners, dependencies, costs, security posture. Mark degraded nodes. Do not invent root cause yet.

check.question: Name at least one degraded component you see.

steps.title: Map components to concerns
steps.prompt: Identify duplicate-prone hop.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Who owns which risk?
teach.explain: Partner → destination/iflow → events → order API.

check.question: Map UI / API / identity / data / integration (as applicable) to component names from the landscape.
check.explanation: Mapping builds a mental model for incident response.

steps.title: Core pattern teaching
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Idempotent intake design
teach.explain: At-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers. Use business keys, DLQ, exponential backoff, cert monitoring.

workedExample.takeaway: Duplicates are design bugs, not bad luck.

revealLevels.title: Nuance
revealLevels.body: Exactly-once is often a myth across systems; idempotency is practical.

check.question: Best pair with retries?

steps.title: Draft architecture hypothesis
steps.prompt: Design idempotent intake with DLQ and cert monitoring.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Multiple options, explicit rejects
teach.explain: Write a hypothesis including major components, trust boundaries, and at least one rejected alternative with rationale. Architecture without rejected alternatives is marketing.

check.question: Describe your design and one rejected alternative.

steps.title: Trade-off matrix
steps.prompt: Compare at least two options across security, cost, resilience, complexity, operational ownership. Pick one.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Score options on security, cost, resilience, complexity, ownership
teach.explain: Cheap designs that skip observability shift cost into incidents. Over-secure designs that block business need iteration. Make trade-offs explicit.

check.question: Write two options and which you pick with one security and one cost note.

steps.title: Identity design checkpoint
steps.prompt: List actors and required permissions/scopes at a high level for this scenario.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Authn/authz is part of the architecture diagram
teach.explain: List actors, role collections/scopes, and how the UI reaches the API (destination auth). Missing identity design becomes 401/403 production theater.

check.question: Name at least one actor and one permission/scope idea.
check.explanation: Identity belongs in v1 design, not as a patch.

steps.title: Bindings & destinations (concept)
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Configuration is code's twin
teach.explain: Service bindings inject credentials into runtimes. Destinations externalize connectivity. Most 'code bugs' in first deploys are binding/destination mistakes.

check.question: A destination primarily stores…

options.text: Connection URL + authentication configuration for callers
HANA column store compression settings only

check.explanation: Connectivity config is a first-class artifact.

steps.title: Configure the solution (sim)
steps.prompt: List config fields to set.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Apply configuration deliberately
teach.explain: Set idempotencyKey=orderId, exponential retry, enable DLQ, rotate cert metadata.

check.question: List the key bindings/config checks you would verify.

steps.title: Happy-path test design
steps.prompt: Describe the happy-path test in 3–5 steps.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Define expected behavior before chaos
teach.explain: Write the user journey that must work: actor, auth, data seen, side effects. Without expected behavior, you cannot recognize failure modes.

check.question: Outline happy path including login/access and successful data/action.

steps.title: Symptoms vs root cause
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Symptoms are not causes
teach.explain: A blank UI is a symptom. 401 is a symptom class. Audience mismatch may be a root cause. Incident skill is moving down the causal chain with evidence.

check.question: Best next step after users report 'app broken'?

options.text: Gather symptoms + telemetry before naming root cause
Immediately rewrite the UI in another framework

steps.title: Failure appears
steps.prompt: Name both symptom classes.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Duplicate orders + TLS warnings
teach.explain: Two coupled defects often co-occur after messy change windows.

check.question: List the user-visible symptom and one technical symptom.
check.explanation: Capture both business and technical views.

steps.title: 401 vs 403 clinic
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Authn failure vs authz failure
teach.explain: 401: not authenticated or token rejected (including audience mismatch). 403: authenticated but missing permission/scope. Mixing them sends you to the wrong runbook.

check.question: Missing Discount.Approve scope typically surfaces as…

steps.title: Gather evidence — logs
steps.prompt: Quote or paraphrase the most important error log line you see.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Read error logs before theorizing
teach.explain: Filter errors/warnings. Note resource IDs and messages. Separate primary evidence from distractors (healthy components).

check.question: What does the strongest error log suggest?

steps.title: Gather evidence — metrics & traces
steps.prompt: Note one metric and one trace span that support your emerging theory.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Correlate pillars
teach.explain: Metrics show magnitude (failure rates). Traces show path. A good hypothesis explains all three pillars without ignoring contradicting evidence.

check.question: Mention a metric or trace observation.

steps.title: Form hypothesis
steps.prompt: Write: If <mechanism> in <component>, then we should see <evidence>.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Falsifiable statement
teach.explain: Write a hypothesis that could be wrong. Include the component and mechanism. Avoid vague 'network issue'.

check.question: State hypothesis with component + mechanism.

steps.title: Eliminate distractors
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Healthy nodes can still waste your time
teach.explain: UI theme changes are almost never order duplication causes.

check.question: A recently successful integration flow means…

options.text: It may be a distractor if the failing path is UI→destination→API
It always proves the UI auth is fine

steps.title: Root-cause diagnosis
steps.prompt: State both contributing causes.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Commit to a cause with evidence
teach.explain: Missing idempotency plus expired partner certificate.

check.question: State root cause using precise terms from this mission.

steps.title: Mitigate business impact
steps.prompt: Write a 3-line status update to business stakeholders + one mitigation action.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Stop the bleeding before perfect surgery
teach.explain: Communicate status, freeze related risky changes, offer workarounds if any, protect data. Mitigation ≠ root-cause fix, but it buys safety.

check.question: Include communication or workaround language.
check.explanation: Communication is part of ops excellence.

steps.title: Least privilege remediation rule
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Never 'fix' security by removing it
teach.explain: Disabling JWT validation, granting Admin.All, or opening anonymous access are not remediations — they are new incidents. Fix the misaligned config with minimum rights.

check.question: Acceptable remediation for audience mismatch?

options.text: Align destination audience with API accepted audience

steps.title: Apply secure fix in simulation
steps.prompt: Describe secure integration fix.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Change the causal config
teach.explain: Enable idempotency + DLQ + rotate cert; backoff retries.

check.question: Describe the fix you applied (or will apply) without disabling auth.

steps.title: Verify recovery
steps.prompt: What evidence shows the incident is mitigated/fixed?
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Prove health restored
teach.explain: Re-check resource health, re-read logs, confirm user journey. Declare victory only with evidence.

check.question: Mention health, log, or user journey verification.

steps.title: Architecture board defense
steps.prompt: Defend delivery semantics and operational ownership of iflows.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Adversarial questions are a gift
teach.explain: Boards attack weak assumptions: CAP vs RAP, identity propagation, retries, residency, cost, rollback, monitoring, ownership. Answer with verified vs assumed.

check.question: Defend identity + one operational concern (monitoring/rollback/cost).

steps.title: Production readiness
steps.prompt: List alert + owner + one runbook step + fidelity note.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Alerts, owners, runbooks, fidelity disclosure
teach.explain: Name alert signals, on-call owner, runbook link (conceptual), backup note, and tell stakeholders what is simulated vs real if demoing.

check.question: Include alert and owner.

steps.title: Prevention control
steps.prompt: Read the teaching panel carefully. When you understand it, continue. You will be checked.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Make recurrence expensive to ignore
teach.explain: Contract tests for idempotency; cert expiry alerts; retry policy review.

check.question: Propose one prevention control (CI check, alert, review gate).

steps.title: Transfer scenario
steps.prompt: How does DLQ help poison messages?
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Same structure, different skin
teach.explain: Same ideas apply to event consumers crashing on poison messages.

check.question: Explain how today's mechanism transfers to the new scenario.

steps.title: Spaced recall
steps.prompt: List 3 concepts + the root cause class in your own words.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Force retrieval
teach.explain: Without notes, restate the three most important concepts from this mission and the root cause class.

check.question: Three concepts + cause class.

steps.title: Reflection journal
steps.prompt: Write reflection covering assumption, evidence, prevention, transfer. Use those words.
successCriteria: Learner engages with concept before proceeding

teach.headline: Metacognition
teach.explain: What assumption failed? Which evidence corrected you? What will you do differently? Consider a break — Odyssey never punishes rest.

check.question: Reflection with assumption/evidence/prevent/transfer ideas.
